outlier

/OWT-lye-er/ - the stress falls on OWT · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Outlier means a person or thing lying far outside the usual range or pattern.

Nine of the ten repair quotes clustered around 400 dollars; the outlier, at 65, came from a contractor who had misread the blueprints.

Example

Charting a decade of checkout data, the library's analyst found the branches bunched tightly together — every one lent between 90 and 140 books a day. Then there was Northside: 460 a day, an outlier so far from the pack that she rebuilt the chart twice, hunting for her own mistake, before believing it. The explanation was simple: Northside kept the county's only Sunday hours.

Outlier is a measuring word — it means a person or thing lying far outside the usual range, and it implies a crowd of ordinary cases to lie outside of. Unlike 'oddity,' it passes no judgment on strangeness: an outlier can be the best, the worst, or merely the farthest, but it is always alone out there.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

exception: An exception breaks the rule — the one case a policy does not cover — though it may sit close to the pattern in every other way. An outlier need not break any rule at all: it is defined by measured distance, lying far outside the usual range. Exceptions defy rules; outliers defy averages.

oddity: An oddity is simply a strange item — it catches the eye, and no measurement is involved. An outlier passes no judgment on strangeness: it is a case lying far from a crowd of ordinary ones, and it can be the best, the worst, or merely the farthest.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

average: the middle of the pack, in every respect

regular: fitting the usual run of cases

Where it sits · how far from the usual pattern — rarity → anomaly → outlier

rarity vs. outlier: A rarity is merely uncommon — a left-handed catcher — and stops well short of an outlier.

anomaly vs. outlier: An anomaly goes further than a rarity — it genuinely departs from the expected pattern — but it stops short of an outlier, which lies measurably far outside the entire range.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — out-

Prefix — out-: outside, beyond

Root — lier

Root — lier: one that lies, is situated

Put it together

Put it together: Out- (beyond) + lier (one that lies) = a thing that lies outside. Surveyors coined it in the 1600s for a mass of rock lying apart from its parent formation; statisticians borrowed the picture for the data point lying apart from the rest, and everyday English now lends it to any person or result far from the pack.

Use the root in a new word: underlie

Use the root in a new word: underlie: No one asked what underlies the board's sudden cheerfulness.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / statistical

Outlier is the number-cruncher's noun, at home wherever there is a distribution to sit outside of — scores, rainfall, salaries. In this unit it pairs with aberrant: aberrant is the adjective for behavior that breaks the pattern, outlier the noun for the case sitting far from it. An exception merely breaks a rule; an outlier is measured by its distance.
